evidence.paraphrase: The host explains that an ancestor made discoveries tied to powers residing in this specific plot of ground.
evidence.quote:
The squire who
succeeded to it in 1768 studied sartain arts and made sartain
discoveries, all connected with influences residing in this particular
plot of ground, and eminently desarving of the strongest guarding.

evidence.paraphrase: The host describes a claimed power of human will to dominate forces, substances, and dimensions of nature.
evidence.quote:
there appeared to reside some
very remarkable qualities in the will of mankind; qualities having a
little-suspected dominance not only over the acts of one
s self and of
others, but over every variety of force and substance in Nature, and
over many elements and dimensions deemed more universal than Nature
herself.

evidence.paraphrase: The host explains a theory that the world can be shaped and dismissed by the intellect of the wise.
evidence.quote:
all the world is but the smoke of our intellects; past
the bidding of the vulgar, but by the wise to be puffed out and drawn
in like any cloud of prime Virginia tobacco. What we want, we may make
about us; and what we don	 want, we may sweep away.

evidence.paraphrase: The ancestor investigated the Indians' rites by bargaining for and learning their secret practices and origins.
evidence.quote:
Thereafter he bargained
with them and exchanged the free access of his grounds for the exact
inwardness of what they did; larning that their grandfathers got part
of their custom from red ancestors and part from an old Dutchman in
the time of the States-General.

evidence.paraphrase: Through the window the narrator sees a past landscape of foliage instead of the modern city.
evidence.quote:
a flash of heat-lightning played
over the scene, and I looked out upon a sea of luxuriant
foliage--foliage unpolluted, and not the sea of roofs to be expected
by any normal mind.

evidence.paraphrase: The host confirms he can display any period of time through the window.
evidence.quote:
"Good God!" I whispered; "can you do that for _any time_?" And as he
nodded

evidence.paraphrase: A second vision shows an earlier version of Greenwich.
evidence.quote:
Again the lightning flashed--but this time upon a scene not wholly
strange. It was Greenwich, the Greenwich that used to be

evidence.paraphrase: A vision of a monstrous future city with flying things and towering terraces.
evidence.quote:
I saw the heavens verminous with strange flying things,
and beneath them a hellish black city of giant stone terraces with
impious pyramids flung savagely to the moon, and devil-lights burning
from unnumbered windows.

evidence.paraphrase: The narrator screams uncontrollably in terror at the future vision.
evidence.quote:
forgetting every injunction to silence I
screamed and screamed and screamed as my nerves gave way and the walls
quivered about me.

evidence.paraphrase: The old man shrivels and blackens under the moonlight.
evidence.quote:
It spread over the old man, too, whether from the
same source or because of his fear and vehemence, and I saw him
shrivel and blacken as he lurched near and strove to rend me with
vulturine talons.

evidence.paraphrase: A shapeless black mass full of eyes bursts into the room.
evidence.quote:
the door fell in
pieces to admit a colossal, shapeless influx of inky substance starred
with shining, malevolent eyes.

evidence.paraphrase: The narrator contrasts New York with London and Paris, claiming it is dead and infested rather than a living continuation.
evidence.quote:
this city of stone and stridor is not
a sentient perpetuation of Old New York as London is of Old London and
Paris of Old Paris, but that it is in fact quite dead, its sprawling
body imperfectly embalmed and infested with queer animate things

evidence.paraphrase: The narrator reacts with a chill upon touching the host's icy flesh.
evidence.quote:
at the first touch of his
ungloved fingers I turned cold. His flesh, though dry and firm, was of
the quality of ice

evidence.paraphrase: The street by which the narrator arrived has disappeared, leaving unfamiliar surroundings.
evidence.quote:
The steep street of my approach was nowhere
visible, and the little I did see succumbed rapidly to a mist that
rolled in from the river despite the glaring moonlight.

evidence.paraphrase: The narrator is found emerging from an unknown place, the site of his ordeal unlocatable.
evidence.quote:
reports could state no more than that I had appeared from
a place unknown, at the entrance of a little black court off Perry
Street.
